{{Quote|The Rebel blockade runner is the pride of the Corellian Engineering Corporation's military vehicles. With its mess of huge engines, it can whoop any jerk-ass Imperial.|Corellian Engineering Corporation advertisement|<ref name="Star Wars: Behind the Magic">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>}}
The '''CR90 corvette''', commonly referred to as the '''Corellian corvette''' or the '''Rebel blockade runner''', also known as an '''Alderaan cruiser''', was a small, multi-purpose [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] manufactured by [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]].

The CR90 had a wide variety of users throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], from [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] to corporations to galactic [[Navy/Legends|navies]], and had a known operational life from at least as early as [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]] to as late as [[137 ABY]]. It possessed the same legendary adaptability as other CEC products, which allowed it to serve in roles as mundane as [[Freighter/Legends|freight hauling]] or as a high-profile [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] escort.

==Characteristics==
[[File:CR90.png|thumb|left|A Corellian corvette]]
A versatile [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the CR90 was used extensively across the galaxy by governments and private interests.<ref name="RASB1">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> The interior of the CR90 featured a modular design to allow for easy reconfiguration of the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]] from one function to another.<ref name="SWSB1" /> Some older model corvettes, like the [[CR70 corvette/Legends|CR70]], could easily be upgraded with retrofit packages like the [[Vanguard c20 retrofit suite|Vanguard c20]] to become CR90s.<ref name="SWI90A">[[Star Wars Insider 90|''Star Wars Insider'' 90]]</ref>

Common configurations included a troop [[Carrier/Legends|carrier]], light escort vessel, cargo [[Transport/Legends|transport]], or passenger liner. Its ease of modification was a trademark of [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|CEC]] and increased the corvette's resale value.<ref name="SWSB1" /> One of the rarer variants could carry starfighters, such as the [[Ession Strike|''Night Caller'']] and ''[[Constrictor]]''.

The weapon systems varied, although the standard configuration mounted two [[Taim & Bak/Legends|Taim & Bak]] [[H9 turbolaser/Legends|H9 dual]] [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] and four single turbolasers.<ref name="SWCCS1" /> CR90 corvettes could carry as many as eight turbolasers, six laser cannons, and four [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]].<ref name="NEGVV1" /> Under the standard configuration, these turrets were unable to hit anything directly behind the corvette's engines, so CR90 corvettes featured a well-known axial blind spot.<ref name="XWS1">[[X-Wing (game series)|''X-Wing'' game series]]</ref>

A common configuration for combat-oriented corvettes consisted of six H9 dual turbolasers.<ref name="SWSB1" /> A similar armament was mounted on the [[CR92a Assassin-class corvette|CR92a ''Assassin''-class corvette]], a successor of the CR90 that was designed exclusively for combat roles.<ref name="TFG1">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

{{IBI|File:BLOC01AB.jpg|A CR90 corvette travels in formation with two [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]].}}
The ship was capable of sustaining acceleration up to 2,100 G<ref name="NEGVV1" /> and could carry 600 passengers.<ref name="SWSB1" /> However, its class 2 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]<ref name="SWSB1" /> was slow compared to many ships of similar size. The standard crew was made up of 8 officers and 38 enlisted crew,<ref name="TSC1" /> but could range from 30 to 165 total, depending on its configuration.<ref name="SW2E1" />

Interestingly, the CR90 could be [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by as few as two people, as shown when [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] flew a series of corvettes bearing the name [[Jaina's Light/Legends|''Jaina's Light'']],<ref name="Routine">{{Tales|2|Routine}}</ref> or even one person if necessary via a steering yoke, as [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] demonstrated when he flew the modified corvette ''Night Caller''.<ref name="XWWS1">''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]''</ref>

The 150 [[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long craft could reach atmospheric speeds of 950 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] per [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]].<ref name="RS I guide" />

==History==
===Republic service===
In the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TDC1">''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]''</ref> the CR90 corvette was introduced and older corvette-models like the [[CR70 corvette/Legends|CR70]] were gradually being refitted into this version.<ref name="SWI90A" /> The Republic CR90 corvettes served in the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] and later in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] when it was reinstated during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The CR90 model was considered a mid-sized corvette in the time before the Wars.<ref name="HNN1" />

===Imperial service===
[[File:Capital_corellian_corvette.png|thumb|left|A corvette in space]]
A dwarf amongst the massive [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], CR90 corvettes were used for diplomatic and escort duty in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. In fleet engagements, CR90 corvettes were often tasked with attacking enemy [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] or fleeing the battlefield with important cargo or intelligence. Prior to the [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|Dissolution of the Imperial Senate]] by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], these corvettes were used by Imperial senators as diplomatic couriers.

===Rebel and fringe service===
Unlike their Imperial counterparts, [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] CR90 corvettes acted as front-line combat ships for the early years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], generally being used as anti-starfighter screens. The ease of acquiring CR90 parts and mechanics made them a good fit for the desperate Rebellion. Its near ubiquity made it a popular choice amongst Rebels, pirates, and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], earning it the nickname "blockade runner" for its ability to slip through Imperial nets. However, it proved ineffective against larger ships such as the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] short of [[Ramming/Legends|suicidal ramming]] attacks unless it was used in large numbers against such a vessel. One example was at the [[Space Battle at Kuat]] when five Corvettes caused considerable damage to the Star Destroyer ''[[Tyranny]]''.

Knowing that the corvette was used by the Rebellion, Imperial authorities often stopped them for inspections on the flimsiest of excuses.<ref name="AoRCR">[[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

{{IBI|File:AlderaansPromise-TCGEoD.jpg|''Tantive IV'', a Rebel corvette, leaves Alderaan.}}
Crime Lord [[Tyber Zann]] acquired CR90 corvettes for his fleet during his corruption efforts in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="FoC" />

===New Republic service===
Following the transition of the Alliance into the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], CR90 corvettes continued to play an important role in the newly organized [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] until phased out of line-duty with modernization efforts like the [[New Class Modernization Program]].

===Later history===
Several CR90s were used to make up a secret retreat in [[137 ABY]].<ref name="SWL25">[[Legacy (2006) 25|''Legacy'' (2006) 25]]</ref> At least two were used during the [[Evacuation of Dac]].<ref name="Legacy 47">[[Legacy (2006) 47|''Legacy'' (2006) 47]]</ref>

==Descendants==
[[File:Sundered-Heart.jpg|thumb|left|[[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']]]]
The CR90 design, itself a descendant of a line of similar vessels, provided the basis for a series of derivative designs and creative refits.

===''Sundered Heart''===
{{Main|Sundered Heart/Legends}}
A well-known example of a significantly modified CR90 was [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']], a corvette modified for extreme speed. With an added set of sublight engines, this vessel was capable of up to four times the sublight acceleration of the original CR90.<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

===CR92a ''Assassin''-class===
{{Main|CR92a Assassin-class corvette}}
[[File:Assassin-class_Corvette_Ring_Planet.jpg|thumb|right|A [[CR92a Assassin-class corvette|CR92a ''Assassin''-class corvette]]]]
Sometime around the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the [[CR92a Assassin-class corvette|CR92a ''Assassin''-class corvette]] began to see widespread use. Commonly known as the "Modified Corvette," the ''Assassin''-class was designed specifically for combat. In its default configuration, it carried six dual turbolasers and one warhead launcher. The Imperial Navy was known to use the ''Assassin''-class in significant numbers.<ref name="TFG1" />

===Corellian Buccaneer===
{{Main|Corellian Buccaneer}}
The Corellian Buccaneer was another militarized corvette class introduced no later than [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]]. It had similar technical specifications to the CR90, but had a stock armament of ten dual turbolasers. One such vessel was used by the [[Dynamic Automata]] company in the [[Pentastar Alignment]].<ref name="TPA1">{{JournalCite|3|The Pentastar Alignment}}</ref>

===Pocket carriers===
Some time after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] captured at least two different CR90 designs capable of carrying starfighters.

====''Night Caller'' and ''Constrictor''====
{{Main|Ession Strike}}{{Main|Constrictor}}
The first was ''Night Caller'', captured from [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]]. Though it was very similar to the CR90 in most respects, it was built from the ground up to serve as a small carrier. The primary changes from the original CR90 design were an enlarged bridge section with a cargo hold that held four TIE/ln starfighters and mines, and a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projector suited to a much larger warship.<ref name="XWWS1" /> The corvette ''Constrictor'' was of the same design and also served in Zsinj's fleet until captured by the New Republic.

====''FarStar''====
{{Main|FarStar}}
[[File:FarStar.jpg|thumb|left|''[[FarStar]]'']]
The second known carrier refit was ''[[FarStar]]''. Originally commissioned in [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]], it was refit by the order of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]]. A large docking bay was grafted onto the vessel's spine, and its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] system was modified to accommodate the new hull shape. It is unclear if this modification was in any way standardized or if it was a custom Imperial design.<ref name="TDC1" />

==== ''Eridain'' ====
{{Main|Eridain}}
Another known CR90 pocket carrier is the Eridain, although the ship isn't described in detail. It is able to carry 12 X-Wings in it's hangar. <ref name="X-Wing: Rogue Squadron">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Main|Tantive IV/Legends#Behind the scenes}}<!-- The Tantive IV article will have most of the BTS info on model design. This article will focus on IU characteristics of the class. -->
The CR90 corvette's design was developed from one originally intended for [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. When that design was rejected for being too reminiscent of [[Wikipedia:Space: 1999|''Space: 1999's'']] ''Eagle Transporter'', it was adapted to become the CR90. The most obvious change was replacing its cockpit area with the distinctive "hammerhead" bridge section. In addition, the [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]] were relocated to the lower hull, with laser cannons being mounted where the pods had originally been placed. This was essential because [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']] had to launch an escape pod while inside the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']]{{'s}} ventral hangar bay.

[[File:Corellian_Corvette_Hologram.jpg|thumb|right|A CR90 Hologram]]
Corvettes have a well-known "blind spot," in that they cannot shoot anything behind their engines, known especially to gamers of [[X-Wing (game series)|''X-Wing'' computer game series]] and used whenever they had to destroy one. This may appear to contradict the very first scene of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']]&mdash;''Tantive IV'' shoots ''Devastator'', right behind her. This may be explained by the fact that ''Devastator'' was a much broader target and slightly above her (although ''Tantive''{{'s}} ventral cannon was also used).

Early [[West End Games]] RPG statistics for the Corellian corvette list its armament as six double turbolaser turrets, despite the corvettes seen in ''A New Hope'' and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] clearly mounting only two such turrets. This was later retconned by describing the heavier armament as an optional upgrade. The CR90 that appears in ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' is armed with only eight laser cannons, although this is a simple game balance issue, as the ship is placed into the anti-fighter role as the Rebel counterpart to the [[Tartan-class patrol cruiser]]. In comparison, the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers mount only four turbolasers instead of the sixty batteries they are supposed to have, while the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 Liberty type Star Cruiser]] is similarly nerfed from 48 turbolasers to four to match the ''Imperial''-class in strength.

Early schematics for the CR90 show a much smaller ship length-wise than the original filming miniature portrays. The reason is unclear, but the trend toward a stunted look continued and affected every incarnation of the ship, from roleplaying deckplans to computer models for the ''X-Wing'' series. The error was propagated even into Revenge of the Sith's portrayal of the Tantive IV as a stunted ship. This was retconned by the Rebel Alliance Blueprints book as being a CR70 corvette, while the much longer Tantive IV is now recognized as the definitive CR90.

In the ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' expansion pack [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|''Clone Campaigns'']], the player via a cheat code, can get a CR90 corvette (then titled "Rebel Blockade Runner") as a playable ship. The cheat code's name was a reference to the Tantive IV.

''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' mentions that Corellian corvettes were an important part of the imperial Support Fleet, but doesn't state the corvette model. The book says that CR70 and CR90 were two of the most common models.<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

According to ''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]'', the sound of the rebel blockade runner in the opening scene of ''A New Hope'' is a mixture of a slowed down World War II AT6 propeller-driven racing airplane and a 747 jet.<ref name="TSOSW">''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]''</ref>
